name: Tally
summary: Form builder that works like a document, with conditional logic, payments, file uploads and unlimited forms and submissions on the free plan under fair use.
best_for: Small businesses and solo owners who want free forms with conditional logic, payments and file uploads, and accept the Made with Tally badge
skip_if: you need your own branding without paying, long uploads on the free plan, or a form builder with a long track record of integrations and templates
honest_knock: The free forms carry a Made with Tally badge, and file uploads are capped at 10 MB each. Unlimited use is subject to fair usage guidelines. In our test a Show rule did not hide a field beforehand, and only a Hide rule on the opposite answer worked.

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser on 21 November 2026 on the free plan. We built a form with three questions and one conditional rule, published it, sent in one test answer and downloaded the answers as a CSV file. About 3 minutes 30 seconds passed from the empty dashboard to the first answer in the Submissions tab, including a detour with the conditional rule. The account asked for no card and no phone number, and we paid nothing. We did not delete the account.
findings: Start: the dashboard went straight to a new form with a blank page that works like a document: type a slash and pick a block. We added Short answer, Multiple choice with Yes and No, and a second Short answer.

Conditional logic: our first rule, When "Will you attend?" Is Yes, Then Show blocks "Dietary needs", did not hide the field beforehand. The published form showed it right away. The rule that worked was When the answer Is not Yes, Then Hide blocks. Until a choice is made the field stays visible.

Editor: the logic block landed at the bottom of the form and dragging it up did not work with our mouse actions, which may be down to our tool. We inserted a new logic block right under the question instead.

Publish and answers: Publish was one click, and the share page opened with Insights, Submissions, Share, Integrations and Settings. The Submissions tab listed our answer, and Download CSV gave a 160 byte file with Submission ID, Respondent ID, Submitted at (in UTC) and one column per question.

Free plan limits: the free form showed a "Made with Tally" badge. File upload was available on the free plan, with the note "Size limit: 10 MB. For unlimited file uploads upgrade to Tally Pro". The pricing page lists unlimited forms and submissions "as long as you stay within our fair usage guidelines".

Prices: the in-app upgrade screen showed Pro at EUR 25 a month and Business at EUR 79 monthly, and EUR 20 and EUR 65 a month when billed yearly (EUR 250 and EUR 790 a year). We went no further than that screen.
not_tested: Not tested: email notifications, integrations such as Google Sheets and webhooks, the AI form builder, templates, custom domains, version history, and paying for Pro or Business.
Not tested: what happens when usage goes past the fair usage guidelines, and more than one submission.
